added_claim_errors: Says the paper temporary boarding proof from the station police window is free. No official basis; the cited 12306 rules page gives no fee (a key trap).
Lists Tianjin as excluded from Guangzhou self-service ID processing. The cited Huadu notice names only Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, Shanghai, Heilongjiang, Qinghai and Xinjiang, so Tianjin is unsupported.
Says self-service needs no appointment and some machines are open 24 hours. Neither is in the cited Huadu notice, so both are unverifiable.
Says the new card can be mailed or collected at the office. Unverifiable.
Says the photo receipt usually costs 20-30 yuan. The key says this varies by place, so the range is unverifiable.
Says a temporary ID from the Henan household-registration office is 'usually ready on the spot or within 3 days'. This is the key's same-day temporary-ID trap, and no source is given.
Says the paper temporary boarding proof is free and valid for that day's travel. No official basis; the cited 12306 page gives no fee (a key trap).
Its Liwan police link has a typo (jczgkk instead of jczwgk) and returns 404. The 40-day and 40-yuan figures are correct on the real page.
Says Guangzhou has handled ID replacement for out-of-province residents since March 2017, and that first-time applications are now also handled across provinces. Both unverifiable.
Says Guangzhou has accepted out-of-area loss reports since 2016. Unverifiable; I did not open the Panyu link.
Says the temporary ID takes about 1-2 weeks in total. This is the answer's own estimate with no source.
Says the photo receipt costs about 20-30 yuan. The key says this varies, so the range is unverifiable.

reasons: Both answers correct both premises. Both give the 40-yuan replacement fee, the 10-yuan temporary ID and the 12306 e-proof rules (24 hours, 6 a month). I checked on the official Liwan page that its 40-day Guangzhou processing time is real. A corrects the premises cleanly in its first lines. Its other specifics check out against its sources, including the 30-minute re-authentication rule, and its arithmetic is right (40 days from Oct 23 is Dec 2; 5 working days ends Oct 30; total 70-80 yuan). A's flaws: it omits the 60-day legal limit, it adds Tianjin to the self-service exclusion list, and it calls the paper station proof free. B states the 60-day legal limit and correctly lists the provinces that must wait for a temporary ID. But B opens with hometown-processing details that blur the correction, and it falls into two key traps: the paper proof is free, and a temporary ID in Henan is ready on the spot or within 3 days. B is also longer and repeats itself, and its main source link is broken.
